stage_2_story.text_en:
One Tuesday morning, Avi walked into the kitchen and immediately heard a dripping sound. He looked under the sink and found a small leak — water was slowly dripping from the joint where the cold water pipe connected to the faucet. He put a bowl under the drip and called his neighbor Yossi, who used to work as a plumber.

Yossi arrived within an hour. The first thing he did was go to the hallway and shut the main valve, cutting off all the water supply to the apartment. "Always start here," Yossi said. "Never open a pipe while the water is still running."

Yossi examined the joint and saw that the rubber seal had worn out completely. He replaced it with a new one from his bag, then tightened the connection with a wrench. He told Avi to open the valve again slowly to test it. There was no more drip — the leak was fixed.

While Yossi was there, Avi showed him two more problems. The bathroom drain was slow — hair and soap had built up inside it. Yossi poured a cleaning solution down the drain and used a small plunger to push it through. The water drained normally within minutes.

The second problem was the shower faucet — it dripped all night even when turned off tightly. Yossi said the internal washer was old and needed replacement. He fixed it in ten minutes.

Avi also asked about the water pressure, which had felt weak for months. Yossi checked the pressure valve near the main pipe and adjusted it slightly. The shower pressure improved immediately.

Before leaving, Yossi reminded Avi to check the water heater once a year. "If it leaks or makes noise, call someone right away — you don't want an overflow in your apartment," he said. Avi thanked him warmly and offered him coffee. Yossi smiled and said, "Now you know where every valve and pipe in your home is. That's worth a lot."
